around.note: Purple box = where and when the number is read: 150 to 50 ms before the peak, half to one blade-distance above the upper blade's sink.

title: Just before a DS, slow (1–4 Hz) activity above the upper blade is weaker with knockout
plain: In the 150 ms before a dentate spike, 1–4 Hz activity just above the upper blade is above its usual level in most controls and below it in most PTEN mice; the more knockout, the lower.
how: ±500 ms around every Halo event and around as many random moments of the same recording (at least 1 s from any event); band power = |Hilbert| of the band-passed CSD (reference-free), 10 ms bins; u = blade-to-blade depth (0 upper blade's main sink, 1 lower; negative = toward CA1). Every event. Per event: 1–4 Hz power from −150 to −50 ms at u −1.0 to −0.5, over the mean of random moments at the same contacts and time (log2; 0 = as at random moments). Per recording: median. Contrast: rank correlation with % knockout, all mice.
ylabel:
1–4 Hz power before the DS, above the
upper blade (log2 over random moments)
why: All mice rho −0.72 (P = 0.0016; Strict set P = 0.0046). PTEN against control P = 0.008; IED− and IED+ each below controls (P = 0.024, 0.048). The before/after version of filter lead 1: something slow is different just before the DS.
against: In most PTEN mice the whole second around the DS sits near the random-moment level at 1–4 Hz, even at the DS itself (panel c), while controls rise toward the DS. So this may be about the random moments (more slow activity at all times in PTEN) rather than about the time before the DS. Tracks the year of recording (rho +0.59). A 1–4 Hz filter also smears the DS backward by tens of ms.
test: Slow (1–4 Hz) power at random moments compared directly between groups (relative to a reference contact far from the dentate); a window ending 150 ms before the peak; mice recorded in the same year.

around.note: Purple lines = when the number is read: 500 to 200 ms before the peak, whole shank.

title: Ripple-band bursts in the half second before a DS2 are more common with knockout
plain: 200 to 500 ms before a DS2, a burst in the 100–250 Hz band shows up more often than at random moments, and more so the higher the knockout: about 29–51% more often in IED+ mice, −15 to +28% in controls.
how: ±500 ms around every Halo event and around as many random moments of the same recording (at least 1 s from any event); band power = |Hilbert| of the band-passed CSD (reference-free), 10 ms bins; u = blade-to-blade depth (0 upper blade's main sink, 1 lower; negative = toward CA1). DS2 events of each recording's winning classifier, DS3 taken out. A burst: 100–250 Hz power (whole shank) above the 95th percentile of random moments for 2 cycles or more. Per recording: share of DS2 events with a burst from −500 to −200 ms, minus the share of random moments with one. Contrast: rank correlation with % knockout, all mice.
ylabel:
Ripple-band bursts before DS2
(share of events minus share of random moments)
why: All mice rho +0.67 (P = 0.009; Strict set P = 0.036). IED+ against control P = 0.008.
against: Tracks the number of events (rho +0.36) and the year (rho −0.42). 100–250 Hz is near the top of what the 1 kHz copy keeps (the decimation filter starts at 400 Hz). Whole shank: where it happens is not resolved here.
test: The same at 5 kHz or 30 kHz on the CA1 rows; planned in new mice.

around.note: Purple box = 50 to 150 ms after the peak, the lower half between the blades. The map shows power; the number is about how well the 30–60 Hz waves line up from one DS1 to the next.

title: After a DS1, low gamma lines up from event to event more with knockout
plain: In the 100 ms after a DS1, between the blades toward the lower blade, the 30–60 Hz waves line up across DS1 events more than chance, and more so the higher the knockout within PTEN.
how: ±500 ms around every Halo event and around as many random moments of the same recording (at least 1 s from any event); band power = |Hilbert| of the band-passed CSD (reference-free), 10 ms bins; u = blade-to-blade depth (0 upper blade's main sink, 1 lower; negative = toward CA1). DS1 events of each recording's winning classifier, DS3 taken out. 30–60 Hz CSD, 50–150 ms after the peak, u 0.5 to 1.0: the power of the average over DS1 events divided by the mean single-event power (1 if the waves line up perfectly, small if they cancel), divided by the same for as many random moments. Contrast: rank correlation with % knockout within PTEN.
ylabel:
Low gamma lined up after DS1
(over random moments; 1 = chance)
why: Within PTEN rho +0.93 (P = 0.0008; Strict set P = 0.017; run 4 P = 0.0002). IED+ 1.1 to 2.6, IED− 0.6 to 1.1.
against: Controls span 0.9 to 2.5 (m2), so PTEN against control P = 0.95. DS1 is a small group in most mice: lining up is easier to see with few events, and the comparison with random moments of the same count only partly fixes that.
test: The same on DS2 (more events); a planned test within PTEN in new mice.

around.note: Purple box = 50 to 150 ms after the peak (compared with 150 to 50 ms before), one to one-and-a-half blade-distances above the upper blade, toward CA1.

title: No longer under 0.05 in run 5. Within PTEN, spiking above the dentate rises after a DS1 more the higher the knockout
plain: Toward CA1, multi-unit spiking in the 100 ms after a DS1 compared with the 100 ms before it goes from slightly lower (m8, lowest knockout) to slightly higher (m5, m34) in perfect rank order with knockout.
how: ±500 ms around every Halo event and around as many random moments of the same recording (at least 1 s from any event); band power = |Hilbert| of the band-passed CSD (reference-free), 10 ms bins; u = blade-to-blade depth (0 upper blade's main sink, 1 lower; negative = toward CA1). DS1 events of each recording's winning classifier, DS3 taken out. Multi-unit activity: the raw 30 kHz signal band-passed 300–3000 Hz and rectified. Per event: log2 of its mean 50 to 150 ms after the peak over its mean 150 to 50 ms before, at u −1.5 to −1.0. Per recording: median. Contrast: rank correlation with % knockout within PTEN.
ylabel:
Spiking after over before a DS1, toward CA1
(log2; 0 = the same)
why: Within PTEN rho +0.64 (P = 0.096). Run 4: rho +1.00 over 8 mice, P = 0.00005. The change is m1 alone: its events moved with its Lock alignment, and its value went from −0.04 to +0.34, off the line.
against: The changes are small (log2 −0.21 to +0.44 over all mice). Controls span the whole range (m59 +0.44). Which rows are 'toward CA1' depends on where the probe sat.
test: Spiking on the CA1 pyramidal layer located by ripples in each mouse; DS2 as well; planned in new mice.

around.note: Purple box = 50 to 150 ms after the peak (compared with 150 to 50 ms before), toward CA1.

title: Toward CA1, ripple-band power drops after a DS in IED− mice and rises in controls
plain: Comparing the 100 ms after a dentate spike with the 100 ms before it, 100–250 Hz power toward CA1 goes slightly down in every IED− mouse and slightly up in every control.
how: ±500 ms around every Halo event and around as many random moments of the same recording (at least 1 s from any event); band power = |Hilbert| of the band-passed CSD (reference-free), 10 ms bins; u = blade-to-blade depth (0 upper blade's main sink, 1 lower; negative = toward CA1). Every event. Per event: log2 of the 100–250 Hz power 50 to 150 ms after the peak over 150 to 50 ms before, at u −1.5 to −1.0. Per recording: median. Contrast: IED− against control.
ylabel:
Ripple-band power after over before,
toward CA1 (log2; 0 = the same)
why: No overlap: IED− −0.028 to −0.013, controls +0.003 to +0.056 (P = 0.006; Strict set the same). Low knockout against control P = 0.017.
against: Very small changes (2 to 4%). Tracks the year of recording (rho +0.49). IED+ mice are mixed.
test: Ripples detected on the CA1 pyramidal layer, counted before and after DSs; planned in new mice.
